Evan (Support): Customer ticket #12345 — multiple customers in Amsterdam report API calls routed to us-west1. High tail latency (~300-900ms), lots of 429 spikes, and a few 401s. They see US IPs from our endpoint. Can we confirm whether DNS/GeoIP flipped for AMS?

Jamal (Infra): Can you paste one failing request id + sample client IP?

Evan (Support): request_id=rid-0a9f3c, client_ip=185.54.225.34 (NL ISP). Timestamp ~2026-03-15T21:10Z. Customer attached `curl` output showing remote addr `34.208.45.12`.

Lisa (Edge): I pulled edge logs for AMS pop. Most hits are normal, but I see a burst of answers from our us-west anycast pool around 2026-03-15T21:08–21:14Z. That window aligns with a CDN partner returning an A record from an unexpected origin.

Ben (Oncall): deploy-bot posted a config change right before that window: `deploy-bot: rolled region-affinity-policy v2 -> v2b at 2026-03-15T21:05Z` — might be related.

deploy-bot: "Region affinity rollout `v2b` applied to edge-routing (canary 5% -> 50%). See run id r-20260315-abc123."

Nina (SRE): Two likely layers: 1) GeoIP DB or CDN partner cache returned wrong country mapping; 2) Upstream resolver/ISP strip of EDNS causing split-view answer (client sees different anycast). We should repro from a Dutch resolver.

Jamal (Infra): Repro steps — from infra: ```
# from a probe in NL (simulated via over ssh)
dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com
# also check EDNS
dig +short +edns=0 @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com
```

Lisa (Edge): On prod I ran:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com
34.208.45.12
```
and from an EU resolver with EDNS client subnet present:
```
$ dig +short +edns=0 @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.com
35.180.22.9
```
So answers vary. Looks like our partner resolver returned the US answer for the ISP in question.

Evan (Support): Customer also reported token auth failing intermittently (401). Could region mismatch cause token validation mismatch?

Nina (SRE): Yes — token validation is region-bound for some private models (we check issuer region claim for Dedicated/private routes). If a request is routed to a region without the customer's key cached, we see auth errors until the downstream token cache warms or fallback header applied. Also retries from their side generated extra tokens -> billing spike.

Ben (Oncall): Immediate mitigation: 1) rollback region-affinity-policy to previous known-good (undo canary), 2) force-purge GeoIP cache on AMS pops and request CDN partner to flush their split-view cache, 3) enable temporary model-agnostic fallback so requests validate across regions. Can infra run steps 1+2 now?

Jamal (Infra): Rolling back canary now.
```
POST /internal/rollouts/region-affinity/rollback r-20260315-abc123
# cli
infractl rollout rollback region-affinity v2b --to v2
```
Done (2026-03-15T21:22Z).

Lisa (Edge): Triggering geoip db reload + pop cache purge on AMS: ```
curl -X POST "https://internal-edge.ams/api/geoip/reload" -H "Authorization: Bearer ***REDACTED***"
curl -X POST "https://internal-edge.ams/api/cache/purge" -d '{"zone":"api.redwood-inference.com"}'
``` Partner notified to purge their split-view caches (ticket sent to CDN ops).

Jamal (Infra): Also traced upstream resolver behavior — the ISP was returning a cached us-west answer due to NAT64/proxying in their network. They have a stale view of our DNS. Recommending we publish a short-lived authoritative SOA bump + TTL reset to force re-resolve.

Evan (Support): Customer tried another request after rollback and reports latency back to ~25–40ms, no 429s, auth OK. They also mentioned billing meter decreased after retries stopped.

Nina (SRE): Postmortem action items: 
- Add telemetry for EDNS client-subnet absence correlated with cross-region answers.
- Short-term: on region-affinity rollouts, block canary expansion to >10% if GeoIP DB age > 24h or partner split-view flag present.
- Long-term: negotiate partner SLA for split-view cache flush API.

Lisa (Edge): I'll attach the dig traces and edge logs to the ticket and mark reproducible case: `repro: dig +edns variations -> US answer on certain ISPs -> auth 401 due to region-key miss`.

Ben (Oncall): Good. Closing loop once partner confirms their purge. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

Evan (Support): Customer confirmed closure. Will add notes to billing team about the retry-induced token usage spike for invoice adjustment review.
